inputs: An operator command, a client configuration naming the requested scopes, and a stored OAuth grant or a fresh authorization code
The two YouTube APIs over HTTPS, reached with the standard library and no third-party client
invariants: A separate program: it imports no Company OS root, so the network-free and no-model checks over those roots keep meaning what they say.
The two halves meet as a sanitized artifact file, never as a shared import; the artifact format is the whole shared vocabulary.
No credential leaves this package: the refresh token is protected at rest and no secret, header or query string reaches the artifact.
An unavailable metric keeps its reason rather than being rounded down to zero, and an incomplete retrieval names the ids that did not return.
Owning this path is governance responsibility, not production authority. Nothing here merges, deploys, publishes or approves.
Standard library only, so requirements.txt is untouched by anything this package needs.
outputs: A sanitized YouTube artifact JSON file carrying channel, video and interval-analytics readings plus retrieval completeness
Secret-free API call telemetry recording that a socket was opened and what it was asked for
purpose: Owns the authenticated half of the YouTube evidence path: the separate program that holds the credential, speaks OAuth and HTTPS, and writes the sanitized artifact that company/youtube reads. It exists outside Company OS so the network-free architecture checks over the Company OS roots stay true.
risks: tools/ is a declared production root, so the production-import check and the research guards apply to every change made here.
It is the only package in the repository that may hold a credential, so a logging or error-message change is a possible secret leak.
Windows DPAPI protects the stored token on Windows only; elsewhere a file-permission protector is used and the weaker guarantee is easy to miss.
company-youtube-connectivity forbids tools/**, so the two halves of the YouTube path cannot be changed under one capsule by design.
title: YouTube fetch client
